title: Net FDI Into India Rises 44% to $13.8 Billion in April-August, RBI Data Show
excerpt: Gross inflows of $54.9 billion and slower outward FDI lifted net FDI from $9.6 billion a year earlier, with services and manufacturing drawing about 73% of equity inflows.
body:
• Net FDI inflows into India rose 44% year on year to $13.8 billion in April-August 2026, from $9.6 billion a year earlier, RBI data in the October bulletin showed.
  • Gross FDI inflows were $54.9 billion in the five months, up from $45.6 billion; August alone brought $11.5 billion gross and $3.3 billion net.
  • The outflows remain large: foreign investors repatriated $23.4 billion and Indian companies invested $17.7 billion abroad in April-August.
  • Financial services, communication services, computer services and manufacturing drew about 73% of equity inflows; Singapore, Japan, Mauritius, the UAE and the US supplied about 81%.

Net foreign direct investment into India rose 44% year on year to $13.8 billion in April-August, the Reserve Bank of India's October bulletin showed, as sustained gross inflows and a slowdown in outward FDI by Indian companies lifted the net figure that has looked weak in recent years.

Net FDI for the first five months of FY27 was $13.8 billion against $9.6 billion in the same period a year earlier, according to the RBI data reported by The New Indian Express and Business Standard. Gross inflows totalled $54.9 billion, up from $45.6 billion. August was a strong month in its own right: $11.5 billion of gross inflows and $3.3 billion net, against a net outflow of $103 million in August a year earlier; July's net figure was $4.1 billion.

"India's gross inward FDI and net FDI flows were higher in April-August 2026, both on y-o-y as well as sequential basis. A slowdown in the pace of outward FDI along with sustained higher gross FDI inflows supported net FDI flows."

— Reserve Bank of India, October bulletin

The two outflows that shape the net number

Net FDI nets off two large flows. Foreign investors repatriated $23.4 billion in April-August through profit remittances and stake sales, and Indian companies invested $17.7 billion abroad — a figure that itself rose 26.5% year on year, with more than half of August's outward FDI going to Singapore, the Netherlands and the US. When either outflow accelerates, the net line sags even in a strong gross year; this period, both were contained enough to let the gross strength show through.

Where the money went

Financial services, communication services, computer services and manufacturing together accounted for about 73% of FDI equity inflows in April-August. By source, Singapore, Japan, Mauritius, the UAE and the United States supplied about 81% of total inflows. The broader external picture was mixed: foreign portfolio investors sold $9.8 billion over the same five months, underlining why policymakers prize FDI — it funds the current account without adding debt and does not reverse in a risk-off week.

What to watch

The next RBI bulletins will show whether the pace holds through the festival quarter and whether repatriation stays contained. For diaspora investors, the composition is the signal: services and financial-sector inflows track the same global-capability-centre expansion that links US firms, Indian talent and diaspora professional networks. The August data also showed the RBI buying dollars heavily — net purchases of $43.26 billion in the month — as it managed the rupee through the West Asia-driven oil shock.
